en.greeting: Hi! Today we imagine: dreams, wishes and situations that aren't real, plus friendly advice with If I were you. Let's start!

steps.title: Imagine: if + past, would
steps.text: You know the first conditional for real possibilities: *If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.* Today: things that are **not real**.
steps.body:
For a dream, a wish, or something impossible now, English uses the **second conditional**:
**if + past simple**, **would + base verb**
*If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.*
**would** = *akan* in an imagined world (you know it from *I'd like*). Short form **'d**: *I'd, she'd, we'd*. Negative: **wouldn't**. Question: **What would you do if …?**
The if-part can come first (with a comma) or second (no comma).

steps.title: Past form, not past time
steps.text: Wait: **had** is past, but *If I had more time* is about **now**. Is the rule broken? No!
steps.body: Here the past form doesn't mean yesterday. It shows the situation is **not real**, far from reality (*jauh dari kenyataan*): *If I had more time* = I **don't** have more time. Indonesian uses a word (*seandainya, andaikan*) and keeps the verb; English moves the verb to the past and uses **would**.

examples.en: If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.
examples.id: Seandainya saya punya lebih banyak waktu, saya akan belajar bahasa Jepang.

examples.en: If Rina lived in Bandung, she'd visit her parents every weekend.
examples.id: Seandainya Rina tinggal di Bandung, dia akan mengunjungi orang tuanya setiap akhir pekan.

examples.en: If I knew the answer, I'd tell you.
examples.id: Seandainya saya tahu jawabannya, pasti saya kasih tahu.

examples.en: I wouldn't pay so much for ojek if I lived near the office.
examples.id: Saya tidak akan keluar uang sebanyak ini untuk ojek seandainya saya tinggal dekat kantor.

steps.title: Too busy to cook
steps.text: Budi works six days a week and eats instant noodles every night. He has no free time.

options: has
had
would have
question.prompt: Complete: If Budi ___ more free time, he would learn to cook.
question.explanation: Budi **doesn't** have free time, so it's imagined: **if + past (had)**, **would + verb**. *has* goes with *will* for real possibilities, and *would* never goes in the if-part.

steps.title: Two traps, and were
steps.text: Indonesian uses *akan* for both **will** and **would**, and that causes two common mistakes.
steps.body:
**1. No would in the if-part.** 'If I would have more money' is wrong → **If I had more money, I would …** (like no *will* after *if* in the first conditional).
**2. Don't mix.** 'If I have a lot of money, I would …' is wrong → **If I had …, I would …**. Keep the pairs: present + will (real), past + would (imagined).
**be → were** for every person: *If I were rich, If she were here, If it were cheaper*. It's a special form for imagined situations; in casual speech you'll also hear *was*.

steps.title: A dream question
steps.text: At lunch, Rina asks her colleagues: 'If you won Rp 1 miliar in a TV quiz, …'

question.solution: What would you do with the money?
question.prompt: Finish Rina's question. Arrange the words: Apa yang akan kamu lakukan dengan uang itu?
question.explanation: A question in the second conditional: **What + would + you + verb …?** Nobody really won: it's imagined, so **would**, not will.

steps.title: Advice: If I were you, I'd …
steps.text: Want to give a friend advice? Imagine you **are** them.
steps.body:
**If I were you, I'd (I would) + base verb** = *Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya akan …*. I'm not you, so it's imagined: a second conditional. It means the same as **You should …**, but sounds more personal.
Negative: **If I were you, I wouldn't …**
Trap: 'If I were you, I **will** talk to her' is wrong → **I'd talk to her**.
**were** is the standard form; *If I was you* is common in casual speech, but write **were**.

steps.title: Advice for Dimas
steps.text: Dimas has a bad toothache. It started three days ago, but he's afraid of the dentist.

options: If I were you, I will see a dentist today.
If I were you, I would see a dentist today.
If I would be you, I would see a dentist today.
question.explanation: **If I were you** + **would / 'd** + base verb. *will* doesn't match an imagined if-part, and *would* never goes after *if*.

steps.title: Real or imagined?
steps.text: Last part: choosing between the **first** and the **second** conditional.
steps.body:
**First** (if + present, will) = a **real possibility** or plan: it can really happen. *If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay home.* (*kalau*)
**Second** (if + past, would) = **imagined**: a dream, very unlikely, or impossible now. *If I won the lottery, I'd buy my parents a house.* (*seandainya*)
Test: you know it's **not true** now (I'm not rich, I don't live there)? → second. A real plan or a forecast? → first. Careful: everyday *kalau* is used for both, so think **real or imagined**.

steps.title: Budi and basketball
steps.text: Budi is 160 cm tall, and he can't change that. He loves basketball, but the office team only takes tall players.

options: If I am taller, I will join the office basketball team.
If I were taller, I would join the office basketball team.
If I would be taller, I would join the office basketball team.
question.explanation: Budi can't be taller: it's **impossible now**, so it's the second conditional: **if + were**, **would + verb**. *If I am … I will* is for real possibilities, and *would* never goes after *if*.

steps.title: A free afternoon in Bandung
steps.text: Budi: 'I'm going to Bandung on Saturday for a meeting. It finishes at 2, so I'll probably have a free afternoon.'

options: If I had time, I would visit Rina.
If I will have time, I'll visit Rina.
If I have time, I'll visit Rina.
question.explanation: Budi will **probably** have time: a **real possibility**, so the first conditional: **if + present (have)**, **will**. *If I had time* would mean he **doesn't** have time, and *will* never goes after *if*.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page. Keep it for the next time you dream out loud or give advice!

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Second conditional
artifact.intro: Second conditional = if + past simple, would + base verb, for imagined situations now or in the future. First conditional = if + present, will, for real possibilities.
rows: If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.
If I knew the answer, I'd tell you.
I wouldn't pay so much for ojek if I lived near the office.
What would you do if you lost your phone?
If it were cheaper, I'd buy it.
If I were you, I'd + verb
If I were you, I'd talk to your manager.
If I were you, I wouldn't + verb
If I were you, I wouldn't lend him money again.
If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay home.
If I won the lottery, I'd buy my parents a house.
tips: The past form shows **not real** (jauh dari kenyataan), not yesterday: *If I had a bigger house* = I don't have one.
**No would after if**, and don't mix: present + will, past + would. *If I were you, I'd …*, not *I will*.
**kalau** (real) → first; **seandainya** (imagined) → second. *If I were you* is standard; *If I was you* is only casual speech.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita berandai-andai: mimpi, keinginan dan situasi yang tidak nyata, plus memberi saran dengan If I were you. Ayo mulai!

steps.title: Berandai-andai: if + past, would
steps.text: Kamu sudah kenal first conditional untuk kemungkinan nyata: *If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.* Hari ini: hal-hal yang **tidak nyata**.
steps.body:
Untuk mimpi, keinginan, atau sesuatu yang tidak mungkin sekarang, bahasa Inggris memakai **second conditional**:
**if + past simple**, **would + kata kerja dasar**
*If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.*
**would** = *akan* di dunia khayalan (kamu sudah kenal dari *I'd like*). Bentuk pendek **'d**: *I'd, she'd, we'd*. Negatif: **wouldn't**. Pertanyaan: **What would you do if …?**
Bagian if bisa di depan (pakai koma) atau di belakang (tanpa koma).

steps.title: Bentuk past, bukan waktu lampau
steps.text: Tunggu: **had** itu bentuk past, tapi *If I had more time* tentang **sekarang**. Apakah aturannya rusak? Tidak!
steps.body: Di sini bentuk past bukan berarti kemarin. Bentuk ini menunjukkan situasinya **tidak nyata**, *jauh dari kenyataan*: *If I had more time* = saya **tidak** punya lebih banyak waktu. Bahasa Indonesia memakai kata (*seandainya, andaikan*) dan kata kerjanya tetap; bahasa Inggris memindahkan kata kerjanya ke bentuk past dan memakai **would**.

examples.en: If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.
examples.id: Seandainya saya punya lebih banyak waktu, saya akan belajar bahasa Jepang.

examples.en: If Rina lived in Bandung, she'd visit her parents every weekend.
examples.id: Seandainya Rina tinggal di Bandung, dia akan mengunjungi orang tuanya setiap akhir pekan.

examples.en: If I knew the answer, I'd tell you.
examples.id: Seandainya saya tahu jawabannya, pasti saya kasih tahu.

examples.en: I wouldn't pay so much for ojek if I lived near the office.
examples.id: Saya tidak akan keluar uang sebanyak ini untuk ojek seandainya saya tinggal dekat kantor.

steps.title: Terlalu sibuk untuk masak
steps.text: Budi kerja enam hari seminggu dan makan mi instan setiap malam. Dia tidak punya waktu luang.

options: has
had
would have
question.prompt: Lengkapi: If Budi ___ more free time, he would learn to cook.
question.explanation: Budi **tidak** punya waktu luang, jadi ini khayalan: **if + past (had)**, **would + kata kerja**. *has* berpasangan dengan *will* untuk kemungkinan nyata, dan *would* tidak pernah ada di bagian if.

steps.title: Dua jebakan, dan were
steps.text: Bahasa Indonesia memakai *akan* untuk **will** sekaligus **would**, dan itu menyebabkan dua kesalahan umum.
steps.body:
**1. Tidak ada would di bagian if.** 'If I would have more money' salah → **If I had more money, I would …** (sama seperti tidak ada *will* sesudah *if* di first conditional).
**2. Jangan campur.** 'If I have a lot of money, I would …' salah → **If I had …, I would …**. Pasangannya tetap: present + will (nyata), past + would (khayalan).
**be → were** untuk semua subjek: *If I were rich, If she were here, If it were cheaper*. Ini bentuk khusus untuk situasi khayalan; saat bicara santai kamu juga akan dengar *was*.

steps.title: Pertanyaan berandai-andai
steps.text: Saat makan siang, Rina bertanya kepada rekan kerjanya: 'If you won Rp 1 miliar in a TV quiz, …'

question.solution: What would you do with the money?
question.prompt: Selesaikan pertanyaan Rina. Susun kata-katanya: Apa yang akan kamu lakukan dengan uang itu?
question.explanation: Pertanyaan dalam second conditional: **What + would + you + kata kerja …?** Tidak ada yang benar-benar menang: ini khayalan, jadi **would**, bukan will.

steps.title: Saran: If I were you, I'd …
steps.text: Mau memberi saran ke teman? Bayangkan kamu **menjadi** dia.
steps.body:
**If I were you, I'd (I would) + kata kerja dasar** = *Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya akan …*. Saya bukan kamu, jadi ini khayalan: second conditional. Artinya sama dengan **You should …**, tapi terdengar lebih akrab.
Negatif: **If I were you, I wouldn't …**
Jebakan: 'If I were you, I **will** talk to her' salah → **I'd talk to her**.
**were** adalah bentuk bakunya; *If I was you* sering terdengar saat bicara santai, tapi tulislah **were**.

steps.title: Saran untuk Dimas
steps.text: Dimas sakit gigi parah. Sakitnya mulai tiga hari yang lalu, tapi dia takut ke dokter gigi.

options: If I were you, I will see a dentist today.
If I were you, I would see a dentist today.
If I would be you, I would see a dentist today.
question.explanation: **If I were you** + **would / 'd** + kata kerja dasar. *will* tidak cocok dengan bagian if yang khayalan, dan *would* tidak pernah ada sesudah *if*.

steps.title: Nyata atau khayalan?
steps.text: Bagian terakhir: memilih antara **first** dan **second** conditional.
steps.body:
**First** (if + present, will) = **kemungkinan nyata** atau rencana: bisa benar-benar terjadi. *If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay home.* (*kalau*)
**Second** (if + past, would) = **khayalan**: mimpi, sangat kecil kemungkinannya, atau tidak mungkin sekarang. *If I won the lottery, I'd buy my parents a house.* (*seandainya*)
Tes: kamu tahu itu **tidak benar** sekarang (saya tidak kaya, saya tidak tinggal di sana)? → second. Rencana nyata atau prakiraan cuaca? → first. Hati-hati: *kalau* sehari-hari dipakai untuk keduanya, jadi pikirkan **nyata atau khayalan**.

steps.title: Budi dan basket
steps.text: Tinggi Budi 160 cm, dan itu tidak bisa diubah. Dia suka basket, tapi tim kantornya hanya menerima pemain yang tinggi.

options: If I am taller, I will join the office basketball team.
If I were taller, I would join the office basketball team.
If I would be taller, I would join the office basketball team.
question.explanation: Budi tidak bisa jadi lebih tinggi: itu **tidak mungkin sekarang**, jadi second conditional: **if + were**, **would + kata kerja**. *If I am … I will* untuk kemungkinan nyata, dan *would* tidak pernah ada sesudah *if*.

steps.title: Sore yang bebas di Bandung
steps.text: Budi: 'I'm going to Bandung on Saturday for a meeting. It finishes at 2, so I'll probably have a free afternoon.'

options: If I had time, I would visit Rina.
If I will have time, I'll visit Rina.
If I have time, I'll visit Rina.
question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang cocok dengan rencana Budi?
question.explanation: Budi **kemungkinan besar** punya waktu: **kemungkinan nyata**, jadi first conditional: **if + present (have)**, **will**. *If I had time* berarti dia **tidak** punya waktu, dan *will* tidak pernah ada sesudah *if*.
